analysis.title: UBS Cash Trading - Main Themes 27th October
key_insights: Europe opens lower: EStoxx -25bps after a US session that tracked sideways into the close (S&P +0.7%, Nasdaq +0.8%), with US futures drifting overnight.
AI IPO filings drove sentiment on Monday: Semis +c2.7%, AI Winners +2%. Hyperscaler earnings are due later this week.
Market-cap outperformed equal weight, and Growth and Momentum recovered. Neoclouds fell on AI infrastructure debt concerns.
AI fundraising continues despite the recent damage to sentiment: Meta plans to raise up to $95bn for its AI buildout, starting with $35bn in common and preferred shares.
Asia trades higher, led by Tech and Memory on the US read across: KOSPI +4.6%, SK Hynix +5.5% on Korean media reports of a further 50-60tr won capital return, Samsung +4.2%.
Nikkei gained more than 2% to about 63,500, with Advantest +10% and SoftBank +7%. China lagged ahead of the Party plenum, with the HSI -0.2%.

Oil is the desk's biggest threat to the early-stage recovery rally. Brent briefly traded above $117 on the risk of renewed US-Iran escalation after the midterms, then eased below $115 as diplomacy resurfaced.
The Fed is expected to hold on Wednesday. The desk sees the real test for the rebound as hyperscaler capex versus monetisation from MSFT, GOOGL and AMZN later in the week.
European banks are weak: SX7E futures -65bps. HSBC earnings were unhelpful for the sector narrative because of commentary on deposit competition (HSBC -5% in HK overnight).
Monday flows finished better for sale (55/45), with turnover c.15% above the HT YTD run rate.
Healthcare was the busiest sector (26% of turnover) and finished better for sale, with supply in pharma.
Banks (15% of turnover) finished better bid on demand for French and UK names, a shift after heavy summer supply amid political headwinds.
Industrials (11% of turnover) saw supply in electricals and maintenance. Technology (10% of turnover) saw supply across semis and software.
Insurance, Food & Bev, Energy and Basic Resources saw supply, while Utilities and Div Fins saw marginal demand.

sector_views.rationale: Busiest sector at 26% of turnover, finished better for sale with supply in pharma. This is a flow observation, not a formal view.
Finished better bid on demand for French and UK names (15% of turnover), following heavy summer supply. SX7E futures were -65bps on HSBC deposit competition commentary.
Supply across semis and software in European cash flows (10% of turnover), while semis rallied c.2.7% in the US on AI IPO filings.

earnings_insights: HSBC earnings (reported 27 Oct) were unhelpful for the European bank narrative because of commentary on deposit competition. The stock fell 5% in Hong Kong overnight.
Hyperscaler earnings from MSFT, GOOGL and AMZN are due later this week. The desk frames the test as capex versus monetisation.

The desk expects a hold, so the Fed is not the main test for the rebound.
